question: Should Discord component callbacks use a 7-day default lifetime and allow an opt-in 30-day maximum for existing deployments?
rationale: This changes how long old visible Discord controls can trigger authorized callback work after upgrade, which is a product/security boundary choice automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept after mechanical refresh
options.body: Update the stale config reference, refresh mergeability, and land the proposed 7-day default plus 30-day maximum if that is the desired Discord policy.

options.title: Keep a shorter/default-compatible policy
options.body: Preserve the 30-minute default or choose a smaller maximum, then align schema, docs, metadata, tests, and proof around that bound.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Close or pause this PR if longer-lived callbacks should remain an explicit per-deployment discussion rather than a bundled default change.

recommendation.title: Accept after mechanical refresh
recommendation.body: Update the stale config reference, refresh mergeability, and land the proposed 7-day default plus 30-day maximum if that is the desired Discord policy.
